<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Beginning to outline the key points about title and meta_title alignment.

`title` serves the on-page headline. `meta_title` drives the browser tab and search results, often adding a site suffix or rephrasing for clarity. They typically differ rather than match exactly.

Matching titles are permitted when intentional, but the convention favors distinct values. The current post aligns with this pattern.
</details></think>

_**Agent (auto-low)**_

No — on this site they usually **shouldn't** match. They do different jobs.

**`title`** is the on-page headline (`<h1>` in `layouts/blog/single.html`).

**`meta_title`** is what goes in the browser tab, search results, and social cards. The template in `layouts/_partials/page-meta-title.html` uses `meta_title` first, falls back to `title` if it's missing, then appends ` | JoRap Notes`.

So the pattern across your blog is:

| Field | Role |
|-------|------|
| `title` | Reader-facing headline on the post |
| `meta_title` | SERP/social title — often tighter or with a hook after a dash |

Your open-source post follows that pattern well:

- **title:** "Why I Focused on Open Source Technologies"
- **meta_title:** "Why I Bet on Open Source - Practical, Not a Manifesto"

The `meta_title` is more specific and angle-driven; the `title` is the cleaner headline on the page.

**When matching is fine:** short, already-clear titles like "Instant Pot Chicken Adobo" where a subtitle wouldn't add much. The blog linter treats `title == meta_title` as "ok if intentional," not an error.

**Rule of thumb:** keep them different when `meta_title` can add context (subtitle, angle, specificity) without making the on-page `<h1>` long or awkward. Keep them the same only when the headline already works everywhere.
